docs/content/how-to/upgrades.md (1)
`10-12`: **Consider clarifying the NodePool downgrade policy for completeness.** The admonition specifically addresses Control Plane downgrades. Since NodePools also expose a `.spec.release` field (line 36), consider whether a note about NodePool downgrade support should be included for consistency. If NodePools follow the same fail-forward policy, mentioning that here would provide a complete picture of the upgrade constraints.
📝 Optional enhancement for completeness If NodePools also don't support downgrades, consider: ```diff !!! important - Control Plane downgrades (moving `.spec.release` to an earlier version) are not supported. Once a HostedCluster has been upgraded, the change cannot be reversed. + Downgrades (moving `.spec.release` to an earlier version) are not supported for either the Control Plane or NodePools. Once a HostedCluster or NodePool has been upgraded, the change cannot be reversed. ``` Alternatively, if the policies differ, a brief note explaining the difference would be helpful.
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. In `@docs/content/how-to/upgrades.md` around lines 10 - 12, Update the Control Plane downgrade admonition to explicitly state the NodePool downgrade policy: check whether NodePool .spec.release supports downgrades and, if it follows the same fail-forward (no downgrade) behavior as HostedCluster, add a short sentence like "NodePools' .spec.release downgrades are also not supported" to the same admonition; if NodePools differ, add a concise note describing the different behavior and where to find details. Reference the HostedCluster admonition and the NodePool .spec.release field when editing docs/content/how-to/upgrades.md so the change is colocated with the existing warning and clearly identifies NodePool behavior. ```
